subject: That-what distinction
source: Lovejoy The Dialectic of Bruno and Spinoza pp145-147
documented_finding: Lovejoy distinguishes inclusion of the being/'that' of phenomena in the Absolute from inclusion of their determinate nature/'what'.
evidence_limit: Does not by itself establish a later formal unit-idea method.

subject: Vedanta worked comparator
source: Lovejoy The Dialectic of Bruno and Spinoza p147
documented_finding: Lovejoy uses Vedanta and the Mundaka Upanishad as an explicit example in which finite being is included in Brahman while finite determinations are excluded from Brahman's own nature.
evidence_limit: Exact edition or translation used for the Upanishadic wording is not identified by this passage alone.

subject: Schopenhauer as modern Vedantism
source: Lovejoy The Dialectic of Bruno and Spinoza p147
documented_finding: Lovejoy calls Schopenhauer's system modern Vedantism and applies the same that/what distinction to Will and appearance.
evidence_limit: Comparative classification does not establish direct historical transmission from Vedanta to Schopenhauer beyond what Lovejoy asserts.

subject: Deussen and Maya comparator
source: Lovejoy The Dialectic of Bruno and Spinoza p144
documented_finding: Testing the Erdmann interpretation of Spinoza, Lovejoy places the resulting illusionist ontology with Schopenhauer and Deussen and invokes the veil of Maya problem.
evidence_limit: The comparison is hypothetical within an exegetical test and should not be converted into Lovejoy's final classification of Spinoza.

subject: Temporal religious stakes
source: Lovejoy The Dialectic of Bruno and Spinoza pp146-147
documented_finding: Lovejoy identifies the serious religious issue as whether spiritual interests stand apart from common natural life or are realized through human business and temporal endeavor.
evidence_limit: Does not reduce the entire metaphysical argument to ethics or social theory.

subject: Contradiction as historical motor
source: Lovejoy The Dialectic of Bruno and Spinoza pp148-150
documented_finding: Lovejoy describes much of metaphysical history as driven by attempts to escape self-contradiction among inherited concepts and assumptions.
evidence_limit: A methodological resemblance to later history of ideas is an interpretive continuity not a formal methodological manifesto.

subject: Influence versus inherited tradition
source: Lovejoy The Dialectic of Bruno and Spinoza pp167-168
documented_finding: Lovejoy acknowledges Spinoza's reading of Bruno and direct influence but says the exact degree matters less because both draw on a longer continuous Neo-Platonic repertoire of methods terms and concepts.
evidence_limit: Does not deny direct influence; it relativizes its explanatory priority.

subject: Explain contradictions not merely detect them
source: Lovejoy The Dialectic of Bruno and Spinoza pp170-173
documented_finding: Lovejoy says adequate analysis must show contradictions' inevitability internal articulation dialectical sources and the philosopher's attitudes toward them.
evidence_limit: Methodological statement is specific to the present historical-exegetical task unless broader comparison is independently made.

subject: Metaphysical otherworldliness
source: Lovejoy The Dialectic of Bruno and Spinoza pp173-174
documented_finding: Lovejoy concludes that absolutist-inclusive metaphysics tends to lapse into a theory of illusion and metaphysical otherworldliness that negates common temporal experience.
evidence_limit: This conclusion targets a family including Western idealisms and should not be equated exclusively with Indian philosophy.

subject: Occidental judging subject
source: Lovejoy The Dialectic of Bruno and Spinoza p174
documented_finding: Lovejoy closes by saying no sober Occidental mind need refute the resulting thoroughgoing metaphysical otherworldliness.
evidence_limit: Phrase demonstrates civilizational marking but does not alone establish a racial or imperial political doctrine.

subject: Wilson retrospective genealogy
source: Daniel J Wilson Arthur O Lovejoy An Annotated Bibliography introduction pp25-26 and entry22 p14
documented_finding: Wilson identifies Religion and the Time-Process and The Dialectic of Bruno and Spinoza as early history-of-ideas essays leading into the Platonic complex later embodied in the chain of being and says the 1904 article anticipates The Great Chain of Being.
evidence_limit: Retrospective secondary interpretation; primary continuity must be established from Lovejoy's own texts.

subject: Wilson pre-1905 corpus sequence
source: Daniel J Wilson annotated bibliography primary-source entries17-26 pp12-16
documented_finding: Wilson's sequence places Lovejoy's 1898 Buddhist philology 1900 French university essay 1902 temporal religion article and multiple 1904 works in one documented publication run.
evidence_limit: Chronological adjacency does not establish a single unified project or causal relation among the publications.
